# osc_backup_schedule (Resource)

Manages scheduled backups of a database instance: whether OSC backs it up, when, and how long it keeps the backups. Supported services: `birme-osc-postgresql`, `linuxserver-docker-mariadb`, `valkey-io-valkey`, `clickhouse-clickhouse`, `apache-couchdb`, `go-gitea-gitea`. Scheduled backups require a paid OSC plan.

Backups are stored in OSC-managed object storage (MinIO). The OSC documentation does not say where that storage is located relative to the database, for example whether it is in another cluster or region, or what happens to the backups when the instance is deleted. For data you cannot lose, also take backups you store yourself, for example with periodic exports.

OSC has no way to remove a backup schedule. Destroying this resource turns scheduled backups off and leaves the schedule and retention in OSC; it deletes no backups. OSC also keeps a schedule after its instance is deleted, so destroy the schedule along with the instance, or an instance created later with the same name is backed up by it. List backups with the `osc_backups` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "db" {
  service_id = "birme-osc-postgresql"
  name       = "mydb"

  sensitive_parameters = {
    PostgresPassword = var.db_password
  }
}

# Back up the database every night at 02:00 UTC and keep the backups for 30 days.
resource "osc_backup_schedule" "db" {
  service_id    = osc_instance.db.service_id
  instance_name = osc_instance.db.name
}

# Weekly backups on Sundays at 03:00 UTC, kept for a year.
resource "osc_backup_schedule" "archive" {
  service_id     = "go-gitea-gitea"
  instance_name  = "mygitea"
  schedule       = "0 3 * * 0"
  retention_days = 365
}

output "db_last_backup" {
  value = osc_backup_schedule.db.last_backup_at
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_name` (String) Name of the instance to back up. It must exist when the schedule is created. Changing it replaces the schedule.
- `service_id` (String) Service of the instance, one of `birme-osc-postgresql`, `linuxserver-docker-mariadb`, `valkey-io-valkey`, `clickhouse-clickhouse`, `apache-couchdb`, `go-gitea-gitea`. Changing it replaces the schedule.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether scheduled backups run. `false` keeps the schedule and retention in OSC but takes no backups.
- `retention_days` (Number) How many days backups are kept. When a scheduled backup completes, OSC deletes the older backups of the instance, including backups taken manually. `0` is what the OSC dashboard stores for a blank retention, which its documentation describes as keeping backups indefinitely. Defaults to 30.
- `schedule` (String) When backups run, as a five-field cron expression in UTC (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), e.g. `0 3 * * 0` for Sundays at 03:00. Fields take numbers, `*`, ranges, lists and steps; month and day names and macros such as `@daily` are not accepted. Defaults to daily at 02:00 UTC.

### Read-Only

- `credential_status` (String) Health of the access token OSC stores to run scheduled backups: `ok`, `renewed` (it was about to expire and was renewed), or `expired` (backups fail until it is replaced; contact OSC support, or disable and enable the schedule). Empty until OSC has checked it.
- `id` (String) Identifier in the form `service_id/instance_name`. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `last_attempt_at` (String) When the schedule last ran, in RFC 3339. Empty if it has not.
- `last_backup_at` (String) When the last backup, scheduled or manual, was started, in RFC 3339. OSC records the time whether or not the backup succeeds; the `osc_backups` data source shows its status. Empty if none has been.
- `last_error` (String) Error of the most recent failed scheduled backup. Empty if it succeeded.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the service id and the instance name, separated by a slash.
terraform import osc_backup_schedule.db birme-osc-postgresql/mydb
```
